reading.title: The Life of a Plastic Bottle
reading.text: Every year, billions of plastic bottles are produced, used, and discarded. A plastic bottle begins its life as crude oil, which is processed into polymers. These polymers are melted and molded into the familiar bottle shape. After being filled with water or soda, the bottle is shipped to a store, where it may sit on a shelf for weeks. Once purchased, its contents are consumed in minutes, but the bottle itself can last for hundreds of years in a landfill. Only a fraction of plastic bottles are recycled. The rest end up in oceans, harming marine life. Scientists are working on biodegradable alternatives, but for now, the plastic bottle remains a symbol of our throwaway culture.

reading.title: The Great Wall of China: Myth and Reality
reading.text: The Great Wall of China, stretching over 13,000 miles, is one of the most impressive architectural feats in history. Contrary to popular belief, it is not a single continuous wall, but a series of walls built by different dynasties over centuries. The most famous sections were constructed during the Ming Dynasty (1368–1644 CE). The wall was designed to protect Chinese states from northern invaders. While it is often said to be visible from space, this is largely a myth; most astronauts report that it is very difficult to see with the naked eye. Today, millions of tourists visit the wall each year, contributing to its preservation and to China's economy.

reading.title: The Power of Music on the Brain
reading.text: Listening to music activates many parts of the brain simultaneously. The auditory cortex processes sound, while the prefrontal cortex analyzes structure and expectations. Music also triggers the limbic system, which controls emotions. This is why a particular song can make us feel happy, sad, or nostalgic within seconds. Studies show that playing a musical instrument can improve memory, attention, and even mathematical ability. In therapy, music is used to help patients recover from strokes and manage stress and anxiety. The universal appeal of music suggests it plays a deep role in human evolution and social bonding.
